quest.title: Sachin's Article
quest.description: There seems to be something else behind what Dori has told you. Why not go and ask her for more information?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: #Well, well, if it isn't {NICKNAME} and Paimon, yet again!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: I have the latest update on the Akademiya Extravaganza. Would you like to hear it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How much is it?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's free! Isn't Lord Sangemah Bay generous?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Do you guys remember Sachin?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The guy who sponsored the Akademiya Extravaganza! Paimon heard that the prize money and Diadem of Knowledge came from him.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Bingo! In fact, not long ago, when I was doing business in the desert, I met an old businessman.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: And guess what I got from him? A dealer's ledger! With it, I can avoid dangerous areas in the desert and go to more places!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Of course, the most important thing is that the ledger mentions Sachin!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It turned out that Sachin had been to the desert to investigate the people's local conditions and customs. He also had cordial exchanges with the traveling merchants in the desert!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Much of the text is lost, but this is a first-hand account of the big sponsor behind the Akademiya Extravaganza! Would you like a look?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay. Let's have a look, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh... this is all hard to understand! Dori, what does this all mean?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: What does this all mean? I'm afraid that if you need it analyzed, it'll cost you an extra million Mora!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Forget it, then!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well, since you're not paying, that'll be all for Dori's special news.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: But let me give you a hint! There should be someone here who's been to a lot of Akademiya Extravaganzas. Perhaps you could talk to them?

talks.objective: Talk to someone at the venue (0/2)

dialogues.speaker: Vasudeva
dialogues.text: Alas, seeing these young children, I can't help but reminisce about the past.

dialogues.speaker: Vasudeva
dialogues.text: The Interdarshan Championship has always been a stage for young talent. Unfortunately, not every genius will be successful eventually...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Vasudeva
dialogues.text: Geniuses are mostly stubborn and cold, and find it hard to understand the pain of others.

dialogues.speaker: Vasudeva
dialogues.text: Empathetic people, on the other hand, often fall into self-doubt and depression.

dialogues.speaker: Vasudeva
dialogues.text: People who are not firm can only stand still, while people who are determined but walk down the wrong path refuse to look back. There's a lot to think about here...

talks.objective: Talk to someone at the venue (1/2)

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: For this year's Interdarshan Championship, my favorite has to be Cyno.

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: Aside from his skills as the General Mahamatra, looking back at the tournament's history, the Spantamad Darshan has the highest percentage of champions.

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: Many people say that the Spantamad Darshan produces many talented people, such as Cyrus, Ruzicka, Lisa, Cyno...

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: The brighter the talent, the sooner the game will lose its suspense. The most exciting competition was still twenty years ago.

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: At that time, my friend also participated in the game, and I went there to cheer for him. The last round was played in Avidya Forest. In the end, no one dared to approach them, and no one knew what was going on in the depths of the forest...

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: Then I heard the Akademiya shut down the competition. Later, the Interdarshan Championship removed many of the events in which people fought to the death, discouraging people from being desperate enough to do so.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is your friend like?

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: Let me think. He's honest and kind, but he's also vulnerable and sensitive.

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: Most of all, he cares about us. When we drink together, our time is filled with laughter and cheer.

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: It's just too bad that it's all in the past now. Among the friends we drank with, some died, some disappeared, some now live in seclusion... They say fate is fickle. Perhaps it's true.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Looks like something did happen twenty years ago... Right, didn't Wiqas tell us to seek him out if we had any questions?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Now that we have time, why don't we ask him?

talks.objective: Go to the Akademiya to look for Wiqas

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: ...That incident from twenty years ago? Why the sudden question? Did you hear any particular information?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We've heard that the diadem seems to have been lost twenty years ago, and some contestant's personality has changed...

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: You seem to know a lot about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wiqas, is there something you're not telling us?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Not exactly. I was five years old when it happened. How could I know?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: But there are things I've never told anyone. I'm actually a part of the Akademiya Extravaganza's planning committee, because of the influence of a senior colleague.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: That senior colleague and I met on a trip. He was... a bit timid, and would always flee and cower somewhere at the first sign of an emergency.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: One day, four years ago, I said to him: "I want to go back to the Akademiya. The Akademiya Extravaganza is about to begin."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And then?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Upon mentioning the Akademiya Extravaganza, he got startled and said something about "it has nothing to do with me."

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: When I said goodbye to him, he insisted on getting a drink with me. After several drinks, he started talking all sorts of nonsense.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I also had too many, and in my drunken stupor, I didn't really hear him that well.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I only remember that he said that he lost the Diadem of Knowledge for a while. He was in charge of the distribution and recovery of the Diadem of Knowledge, and that he nearly had a heart attack upon realizing that the diadem was missing. Fortunately, he finally found it in a tree hole.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Like the one we saw before...

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: He said that the Diadem of Knowledge is a very valuable treasure, which is recorded in many ancient books. Legend has it that it was built by a famous craftsman in ancient times, and carries a secret that no one knows.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Sachin had entrusted the Akademiya to safeguard the diadem, after all. If my senior was responsible for the diadem's disappearance, he could not afford to pay for it with his meager wealth.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Even if the loss was temporary, no one should know of it, lest the Akademiya find him guilty of gross negligence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So he covered it up?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Yes. It seems that he also said that many people came to inquire about it, including children. But he said that the diadem had never been lost.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: But he was so scared that when things blew over, he quit his job and left the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I drank too much that night, and when I woke up the next day, he was gone. The more I thought about it, the more I had a bad feeling that issues would crop up in the Akademiya Extravaganza if entrusted to someone like him.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I didn't have a job at the time, so I joined the Akademiya Extravaganza Planning Committee. I tried to investigate things on the inside too, but I couldn't find anything.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: And the diadem was found, and the man whose personality was said to have changed, was dead, and there was nothing to be found.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: Still, twenty years is still a long time. Long enough that the people involved from the beginning no longer remember nor care.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: That's all I know. If you're curious, keep investigating and maybe one day, you'll discover the truth...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's easy for you to say. We don't have much to go on. Do you have any more information? Like where the senior colleague went?

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I haven't heard from him. Later, I also went to the desert to look for him, but in the vast desert, it was almost impossible to run into him.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: To make up for it, I do have some information on Sachin. Would you like to hear it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Emm... sure! Tell us!

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: When I was traveling, I did so with an Eremite commander. While we were chatting, he said he came into possession of an article written by an Akademiya researcher.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: He seemed to think it was something precious, and refused to show it to anyone, only to let me peek at it at my request. I only caught a glimpse of it, but I saw that it was signed by Sachin.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: I didn't know who Sachin was, nor did I care. After joining the Akademiya Extravaganza Planning Committee, I found out that he was an important member of the Vahumana Darshan who sponsored the event.

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: If you're interested, you can find the Eremite commander in the desert. He's usually in the Valley of Dahri.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Information related to Sachin? Alright, let's go take a look.

talks.objective: Ask the mercenary about Sachin's article

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: What do you want?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! This guy looks real fierce!

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: Either say your piece, or leave. I have no time for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we heard that you have Sachin's article on you, so we were wondering if we could have a look.

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: ...Are you kidding me?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: No! Why would you ask that?

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: It seems like you guys really don't know. Some time ago, I had the article appraised. Turns out, it's nothing more than a personal travel journal, and is of little value.

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: He hired my father to keep him safe. That Sachin fellow would often walk, ask, write, and mumble.

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: There was one time his papers were blown away by the wind. He said it was no big deal. My father, however, thought that things written by intellectuals must be valuable, so he looked around for them at night with a torch.

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: None among my family can read. My father cherished this article and then passed it onto me. I had no idea it was completely worthless.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds unfortunate... but do you still have it?

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: Yes. You want to have a look? You can look at it as much as you want. Since it's not worth anything, there's no need for me to be so stingy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the article that Sachin wrote? Eh... to be honest, Paimon can't make sense of any of it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... judging from the crummy handwriting, Paimon can't say exactly why, but Paimon has the feeling he was going through a tough time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, we're done reading it. Thank you very much!

dialogues.speaker: Suhayb
dialogues.text: You're welcome. It's not worth any money, but I'm going to keep it anyway. After all, my father entrusted it to me. Come see me again if you want to look at it again.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Well... Here's some food for thought. Why did Sachin sponsor the Akademiya Extravaganza?

dialogues.speaker: Vasudeva
dialogues.text: Ah, to be young...

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: Time will erase all traces of one's existence.

dialogues.speaker: Huvishka
dialogues.text: I have long forgotten much of the merry times during my days as a student. Even now, I'm unsure of what exactly I'm reminiscing about. Perhaps, I'm just reluctant to admit that I'm getting old...

dialogues.speaker: Wiqas
dialogues.text: So, have you got any news?
